source: Review round 2, R2B-8 (header views over the server's request); RFC 0006 §5.3.1
statement: Nothing reads the server's request after the response. Headers, cookies and the address are read as a view over the server's request only while the request is being decided; whatever outlives it (a decision event and what a listener keeps of it, an audit record, a shadow replay, a security context an application holds) carries copies made before the response.
guards: runtime:CheckAfterResponseTest#a check admitted before the end reads the copy after the server recycles the request
runtime:CheckAfterResponseTest#an ended request admits no check and never goes back to the server
runtime:CheckAfterResponseTest#the end waits for a check that is copying the headers
spring-boot:RealServerAfterResponseTest#a listener and the audit record read after the response what the request carried
spring-boot:RealServerAfterResponseTest#a security context kept after the response answers what the request carried, and admits no check
spring-boot:RealServerFactsParityTest#Tomcat refuses its request after the response
